Convexity/increase of z^t (t>=1) majorizes a^t+b^t by 1+(1+u)^t, with equality in the explicit hexagonal norm. Differentiating F_t(u) gives derivative sign D_t(u)=(1-u)(1+u)^{t-1}-u; its unique root follows from monotonicity of T(u)=1+log[u/(1-u)]/log(1+u). At equality the chord sum is 3 and published Radon rigidity forces an affine-regular hexagon. The order-2 value (3+sqrt5)/4, monotone t, and limiting t(2-B(t))=4 log 2 follow by explicit scalar algebra. The compactness/equality argument covers t=1 and endpoints. This relies explicitly, not silently, on the quoted published Radon-plane geometric theorem. Inspected source check.py verifies finite rational hexagonal identities and scalar samples; these are corroboration, not the infinite proof.
